AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MAY 3, 2022
UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE, MEETINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF
ASSEMBLY BILL 361, WHICH ALLOWS COUNCIL MEMBERS TO PARTICIPATE FROM A REMOTE
LOCATION WITHOUT LISTING A PHYSICAL LOCATION. TO PROVIDE COMMENTS DURING A MEETING:
YOU MAY ATTEND THE MEETING, SEND AN EMAIL TO: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, OR JOIN THE
ZOOM MEETING BY CALLING: (669) 900-6833 OR USING THE ZOOM APP WITH THE FOLLOWING LINK:
https://us02web.zoom.us/j/7095732685; MEETING ID: 709 573 2685. THE MEETING MAY BE VIEWED
THROUGH ZOOM, FIOS CHANNEL 32 OR CHARTER CHANNEL 3, OR ON THE CITY'S WEBPAGE AT:
https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/meeting-agendas-393.
  6:15 PM
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Rick Ramirez, Mayor
  Ana Valencia, Vice Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Councilmember
  Jennifer Perez, Councilmember
  Margarita L. Rios, Councilmember
  Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
  the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
  subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
  minutes.

  Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
  certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
  matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

  Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

  Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
  meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
  devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
  documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
  Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
  that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

  Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
  has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

  Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
  during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
  telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING – 5:00 p.m.
 CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Ramirez

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION

  I.  PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957.6; CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR.
  Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager; regarding negotiations with the
  Norwalk City Employees Association.

  II.  PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957.6; CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR.
  Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager; regarding negotiations with the
  Norwalk Association of Management Employees.

  III.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – ANTICIPATED  LITIGATION  PURSUANT
  TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54956.9(d)(4) in one case.

RECESS

  REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Ramirez

INVOCATION
  Pastor Joy Clement
  Rock of the Nations Church

FLAG SALUTE
  Syrena Hernandez, 3rd grader
  Studebaker Elementary School

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS
  City Council to proclaim May as Traffic Safety Awareness month in the City of Norwalk.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  COVID-19 Update.

  2.  Congresswoman Linda T. Sanchez to present a check in the amount of $1.72 million to the City for
  Smart and Safe WiFi Zones.

  3.  Department Highlights – Engineering Division.
   4.  La Jara Brewing Company Ribbon Cutting Event video.

  5.  Arbor Day Tree Planting Event video.

  6.  Bi-Weekly in Review.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  WAIVE READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES ON THE AGENDA - Staff recommends City Council
  waive reading in full of all ordinances on the agenda and declare that said titles which appear on the
  public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further reading waived.

  2.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meeting of April 19,
  2022. 825-04

  Minutes

  3.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the period April 3, 2022 – April 16,
  2022, in the total amount of $962,483.25. 630

  Report

  4.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period April
  12, 2022 - April 25, 2022 in the total amount of $1,396,938.46. 640

  Report

  5.  CLAIMS AGAINST THE CITY – Staff recommends City Council deny the claims filed by Dario Peralta
  and Peter Swearinger. 830-

  Report

  6.  PLANNING COMMISSION SYNOPSIS – APRIL 27, 2022 - No action is required. 320

  Report

  7.  ORDINANCE NO. 22-1730 - AMENDING TITLE 10 OF THE NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE TO
  INCORPORATE GUIDELINES FOR PARKING PERMITS – Staff recommends City Council accept for
  second reading and adopt Ordinance No. 22-1730, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  AMENDING CHAPTERS 10.04, 10.08, 10.09, 10.10, AND 10.12 OF TITLE 10 OF THE NORWALK
  MUNICIPAL CODE TO INCORPORATE ADMINISTRATIVE AND PROGRAM GUIDELINES
  PERTAINING TO PARKING PERMITS FROM THE ADOPTED PARKING ACTION PLAN. 1050-02

  Report

  8.  ORDINANCE NO. 22-1731 – AMENDING CHAPTER 8.56 OF THE NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE
  ADDING NEW AND AMENDING CURRENT STANDARDS FOR FORECLOSED AND ABANDONED
  PROPERTIES - Staff recommends City Council accept for second reading and adopt Ordinance No.
  22- 1731, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF NORWALK AMENDING CHAPTER 8.56 OF THE
  NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE TO INCLUDE STANDARDS FOR BOARDING, FENCING, AND
  MAINTAINING VACANT PROPERTIES AND AMENDING STANDARDS FOR FORECLOSED AND
  ABANDONED PROPERTIES. 305-03-04

  Report

  9.  AGREEMENT - FLEET MAINTENANCE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM - Staff recommends City Council
  approve an agreement with Avail Technologies, Inc., for a Fleet Maintenance Management System, in
  an amount not to exceed $122,552 for a five year term starting July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2027;
  and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement and any amendments provided there is
  funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 1120-10
   Report

  10. AGREEMENT – AUDITING SERVICES - Staff recommends City Council approve an agreement with
  Vasquez +Company, LLP to provide financial auditing services for four years ending June 2025, with
  an option to extend for two additional one-year periods ending June 30, 2026 and June 30, 2027; and
  authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement and any additional amendments, provided there
  is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 606-01

  Report

  11. AGREEMENT - ELECTRONIC BID MANAGEMENT SOFTWARE – RESOLUTION NO. 22-23 –
  BUDGET AMENDMENT - Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  adopt Resolution No. 22-23, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2021/22 ADOPTED
  BUDGET TO APPROPRIATE FUNDING FOR THE ELECTRONIC BID SOFTWARE USING
  AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN ACT’S STATE AND LOCAL FISCAL RECOVERY FUNDS; and

  b.  approve an agreement with PlanetBids; and authorize the City Manager to enter into the
  agreement, and any amendments provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in
  a form approved by the City Attorney. 634-04

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  12. ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200 RESOLUTIONS

  Report

REPORTS

13. RESOLUTION NO. 22 -24 BUDGET AMENDMENT - WOMEN?S RECOVERY RESPONSE GRANT
  PROGRAM AGREEMENT APPROVAL - Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  adopt Resolution No. 22-24, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK,
  AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2021/22 ADOPTED BUDGET TO
  APPROPRIATE FUNDS FOR THE WOMEN’S RECOVERY RESPONSE GRANT PROGRAM TO
  FUND THE LEADERSHIP AND ADVOCACY FOR THE DIRECTION OF YOUNG WOMEN
  MENTORSHIP PROGRAM, in the amount of $25,000; and

  b.  approve an agreement with the California Commission on the Status of Women and Girls, to provide a
  Women’s Recovery Response Grant Program in the amount of $25,000 for Fiscal Year 2021/22; and
  authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement and any amendments provided there is funding
  in budget and it is within the City Manager’s signing authority, on behalf of the City, in a form approved
  by the City Attorney. 425-04

  Report

14. MOBILE SURVEILLANCE TRAILERS – Staff recommends City Council authorize the purchase of two
  surveillance trailers from Wireless CCTV LLC, in the amount of $85,000. 950

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated April 28, 2022.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
